title: Customer Runway & Exit Criteria: Signal Gating for Contracted Deliverables
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Top accounts request roadmap commitments late in the cycle, often conflating feature asks with contract SLAs. This causes scope churn, misaligned engineering allocations, and executive escalations. Current intake lacks a clear 'runway' definition (time-to-decision vs time-to-delivery) and no explicit exit criteria for queued commitments.

Goal: Create an operational playbook and enforcement mechanism that gates incoming top-account signals into three lanes (Expedite, Evaluate, Deflect) based on signal scoring, contractual constraints, and delivery runway. Define exit criteria for each lane so customers know when a request will be accepted, declined, or require a new commercial commitment.

Scope:
- Design a signal scoring rubric (account weight, ARR, legal/compliance blocker, product fit, feasibility estimate).
- Define explicit runway windows (2-week triage, 8-week committed delivery, 12+ week roadmap candidate) and associated customer communications.
- Create templated customer responses and SLA language for each lane.
- Implement lightweight console/CRM flags and dashboard slices to show runway state, owner, and next decision date.
- Align PL/Eng on decision authority, fallback policies (auto-escalate to Exec Advocate after 14 days), and compensation/engineering credit mechanics.

Non-goals: Automating engineering prioritization algorithms; replacing contract/legal negotiations.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A documented playbook published in Confluence with rubric, lane definitions, communication templates, and decision matrix.
2) Dashboard prototype in Console showing lane, owner, next decision date, and committed delivery window for 90% of active top-account requests.
3) Two pilot top-account requests processed using the new playbook with documented outcomes and customer-facing communications.
4) Stakeholder sign-off from Sales (VP Sales), Legal (Head of Legal), and Eng (Head of Platform).

Success metrics (OKR-aligned):
- Reduce average time-to-decision for top-account roadmap asks from 21 days to 7 days (OKR-CustomerTrust-1).
- Decrease unexpected scope slippage on committed items to <10% per quarter.
- Increase Sales NPS for roadmap requests by 15 points in pilot accounts.

Risks & mitigations:
- Perceived rigidity: include a flexible 'canary' clause allowing negotiated exceptions with Exec Advocate sign-off.
- Engineering capacity misallocation: require feasibility estimate and ENG-20154 (capacity tagging) integration before lane promotion.
- Legal/compliance blockers: immediate routing to Legal lane with explicit hold reasons and next-action owner.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): Draft rubric and templates, internal review with Sales/Legal/Eng.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): Build dashboard flags and integrate with CRM tags; pilot with 3 top accounts.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Collect feedback, iterate templates and scoring thresholds.
Phase 4 (ongoing): Expand to all top accounts and bake into quarterly renewal playbook.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Lena Park (owner), Ava Martinez (PM sponsor)
- Sales: Priya Desai (VP Sales)
- Engineering: Rohan Gupta (Head of Platform)
- Legal: Marco Alvarez (Head of Legal)
- Customer Success: Mei Chen (Director)

Deliverables:
- Confluence playbook + one-pager for execs
- Console dashboard prototype (owner: Eng roadmap team)
- Communication templates (email, contract addendum language)
- Pilot outcomes report with recommendations for Q3 roadmap gating

Notes: This playbook should integrate with existing admission gates described in PM-9401 but introduce clearer temporal commitments and explicit exit criteria to reduce escalations and speed decisions.
